problem: Embodied agents need to ground natural language in visual perception and actions, but prior work has weak visual description generation and evaluation, and VLN agents suffer from poor generalization and data scarcity in unseen environments.
motivation: Human-machine communication requires agents that can both describe and understand the visual world and act on language commands in 3D environments. The dissertation is driven by the observation that generalization and limited data are key bottlenecks for language-vision-action grounding.
key_idea: Close the loop between language, vision and action by developing scalable visual description methods and VLN methods (counterfactual thinking, transfer, multitask and agnostic learning) that generalize to unseen environments.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation-level evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that semantics and external knowledge help generalizable visual description, and that learning strategies such as counterfactual, transfer, multitask and agnostic learning address VLN data scarcity and generalization.
method: Visual description: scalable learning approaches using semantics and external knowledge to generate coherent, fine-grained, generalizable descriptions
Adversarial reward learning (AREL): learns rewards for visual storytelling to overcome limitations of automatic metrics
VATEX: a multilingual video-and-language dataset going beyond monolingual grounding
Vision-language navigation: systematic study of associating human commands with visual perception to navigate 3D environments
Generalization methods for VLN: counterfactual thinking, transfer learning, multitask learning and environment-agnostic learning to tackle data scarcity
results: The abstract reports no quantitative results. It claims the methods improve generalization of embodied navigation agents and generate coherent, fine-grained, generalizable descriptions.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details and numbers cannot be verified
The dissertation spans multiple topics, so the navigation part may be less focused
